messages:
alex_m: heads-up — customer tenant-42 reporting ~30% 5xx (504/gateway timeouts) on hosted API since 11:10 PST. High-impact, hitting production routes for short-text generation. escalating to incidents.
support_escalations: ticket#12345 created, customer attached curl traces and our request_ids. They say spikes correlate with bursts. here are sample errors: 
  {"status":504,"error":"gateway_timeout"}
sre_oncall: I can see elevated queue depth on inference-prod-us-west-2; controller logs show scale-up attempts but pods remain unready. KEDA logs: "Scale request suppressed: metric auth failed" around 11:09.
maya_s: grabbing keda/metrics logs now. quick grep shows 401 from metrics endpoint after token rotate: 
  2025-05-12T18:09:12Z keda-operator INFO fetch metrics -> 401 Unauthorized
  2025-05-12T18:09:13Z keda-operator INFO treating as zero activity
alex_m: ah — if KEDA sees zero activity it won't scale, and we end up with cold pods and warmup delays -> gateway timeouts. any evidence of prewarm disabled on this scaledobject?
maya_s: yep, scaledobject annotations: 
  annotations:
    redwood.com/prewarm: "false"
    autoscale.keda.sh/cooldown: "300"
  readiness logs from pods show model init taking 50-70s and liveness probe flapping.
sre_oncall: also noticed billing/broker returned 429 for tenant-42 earlier (11:08-11:12). billing_bot: do we have token rotation or billing throttle events?
billing_bot: billing-service: tenant-42 hit token quota at 2025-05-12T18:08:45Z. Returned 429 for /usage/metrics fetch attempts. Rotation job ran at 18:05 and succeeded, but the metrics-client used stale creds until 18:09.
support_escalations: customer note — they retried and saw temporary improvement when we manually bumped replicas. They want root cause and repro steps.
sre_oncall: current mitigation: manually scaled inference pool -> kubectl scale deployment/inference-pool -n prod --replicas=10; set scaledobject cooldown to 30s and set prewarm=true on affected pool. That reduced 5xx rate to ~2% in 10m.
maya_s: repro steps for runbook (staging):
  1) rotate metrics token: POST /ops/rotate-metrics-token (dev only)
  2) run load generator: ./tools/loadgen --concurrency 60 --qps 120 --tenant tenant-42
  3) watch keda operator logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/keda-operator | grep metrics
  Expectation: if metrics-client returns 401/429, KEDA reports 0 and scale doesn't happen -> queue backlog and 504s within ~30s
devops_bot: suggested quick fix script applied: 
  kubectl patch scaledobject inference-pool -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/metadata/annotations/autoscale.keda.sh~1cooldown","value":"30"},{"op":"add","path":"/metadata/annotations/redwood.com~1prewarm","value":"true"}]'
sre_oncall: root cause hypothesis: token rotation produced a brief window where metrics scraping failed (401) and billing service rate-limited metrics client (429). KEDA interpreted lack of metric as no activity and suppressed scale-ups. Combined with disabled prewarm and long model-init -> high probability of 504s on burst traffic.
alex_m: action items: 1) patch KEDA client to retry on 401/429 and fallback to HPA scale signal (ticket infra-987). 2) add guard in scaledobject to force prewarm=true for high-traffic tenants. 3) update runbook and add alert when metrics-client gets >=3 auth errors in 1m. assign.
support_escalations: telling customer temporary workaround (pinned dedicated capacity) and ETA for fix: 48h. customer accepted but requests postmortem.
maya_s: capturing logs and timeline for postmortem: ordering events -> token rotation 18:05; billing 429 spike 18:08-18:09; KEDA 401/429 errors 18:09; queue backlog and 504 spike 18:10-18:15; manual scale applied 18:13; error rate drops 18:16.
sre_oncall: I'll open infra-987 and set priority P1. attaching diagnostic commands used: 
  kubectl get scaledobject inference-pool -n prod -o yaml
  kubectl logs deploy/keda-operator -n kube-system --since=1h | grep -E "401|429|Scale request"
  kubectl get hpa -n prod
alex_m: thanks everyone. escalation note: include repro script and advise customers to use dedicated for critical SLAs until fix deployed. will follow up in postmortem channel. :thumbsup:
support_escalations: closing incident channel update; cc'ing account team.
